tool.name: MSOutputComparison
tool.description: compares two MS pipeline outputs (ions, masses, retention times, intensities)

section.name: inputFiles1
section.title: 📁 Files from the first MS pipeline

param.name: variablemetadata1
param.label: VariableMetadata — Pipeline 1
param.help: The variableMetadata file produced by your first MS pipeline (typically from groupChromPeaks or fillChromPeaks).

param.name: datamatrix1
param.label: DataMatrix — Pipeline 1
param.help: The dataMatrix file corresponding to the same MS pipeline.

section.name: inputFiles2
section.title: 📁 Files from the second MS pipeline

param.name: variablemetadata2
param.label: VariableMetadata — Pipeline 2
param.help: The variableMetadata file produced by your second MS pipeline.

param.name: datamatrix2
param.label: DataMatrix — Pipeline 2
param.help: The dataMatrix file corresponding to the same second MS pipeline.

param.name: wf1_name
param.label: Name of the first pipeline (used in the report)
param.help: Choose a short, descriptive name. This name will appear in the PDF report charts.

param.name: wf2_name
param.label: Name of the second pipeline (used in the report)
param.help: Choose a short, descriptive name for the second pipeline.

param.name: mz
param.label: Maximum m/z tolerance (in Dalton)
param.help: Maximum mass (m/z) distance for an ion from Pipeline 1 to be matched with an ion from Pipeline 2. Typical values: 0.01-0.05 Da for high-resolution instruments. Increase this value if too few ions are paired. This value is also used for the heatmap axis scale.

param.name: rt
param.label: Retention time (RT) tolerance
param.help: Maximum retention time difference for matching two ions. The unit depends on your MS pipeline: if RT data are in minutes, enter a value in minutes (e.g. 0.25 min). If in seconds, enter a value in seconds (e.g. 15 s). Check the unit in your variableMetadata file. This value is also used for the heatmap axis scale.

param.name: corr_split
param.label: Correlation split threshold for zoom histograms (r)
param.help: Pearson r threshold used to split the two analytical zoom histograms (charts ② and ③ in Section 5 of the report). The lower-half zoom displays ions with r from the minimum up to this threshold; the upper-half zoom displays ions from this threshold up to the maximum. Adjust to focus on a different range of correlations — for example, use 0.7 to inspect the boundary between moderate and strong correlations.

param.name: mz_col
param.label: Name of the m/z column in the variableMetadata
param.help: Exact name of the column containing the masses (m/z) in your variableMetadata files. Only change this if your file uses a different column name.

param.name: rt_col
param.label: Name of the RT column in the variableMetadata
param.help: Exact name of the column containing the retention times in your variableMetadata files. Only change this if your file uses a different column name.

.. class:: infomark
**Support:** https://community.france-bioinformatique.fr/c/galaxy/10
----
********************** MS Output Comparison ********************** =========== DESCRIPTION ===========
MSOutputComparison is a tool designed to compare the outputs (variable metadata and data matrices) of two different MS workflows by uniquely-coupling ions of one output to those of the other output, based on a retention time (RT) and m/z tolerance given by the user.
The algorithm identifies these ions as follows:
1. A tolerance of m/z and RT are specified by the user in the interface, 2. For each ion in the first dataset, a list of “candidates” is created, i.e. ions in the second dataset that are “in the neighborhood” defined by the tolerances, 3. For each ion in the first dataset, the m/z differences with each of its candidates are calculated. A table is then created, each line of which is of the form [ion (dataset 1) / one of its candidate ions (dataset 2) / mass difference], 4. This table is sorted in ascending order of mass difference, 5. Two empty blacklists are initialized, one for dataset 1 ions and one for dataset 2 ions, as well as an empty association table, 6. Starting with the smallest difference: - If neither of the two ions is found in its respective blacklist, then they are added to its blacklists and entered with their characteristics in the association table. - Otherwise, if they are not at the terminal end, we move on to the next difference. 7. Ions that have not been matched as a result of this procedure are added to the association table as “no match”.
This algorithm guarantees that each ion in a dataset is associated with the ion in the other dataset that is closest to it (in this case, by mass)
======================== WHAT DOES THIS TOOL DO? ========================
This tool compares the outputs of **two different MS pipelines**, potentially obtained from the same samples. It addresses questions such as the following:
- *"Do variations in the pre-processing parameters influence the detected ions?"* - *"Do my two sets of MS parameters yield equivalent results?"* - *"What proportion of ions is shared between the two pipelines?"*
----
====================== INPUT FILES ======================
For each MS pipeline, you need **two files** produced by the last step of your workflow:
1. **variableMetadata** (tabular file): contains the list of detected ions with their mass (m/z) and retention time (RT) 2. **dataMatrix** (tabular file): contains the intensities of each ion per sample
These tables should match the W4M's 3-tables format (see here for more information).
.. class:: warningmark
To benefit from intensity comparisons, both pipelines must have been applied to at least a few shared samples (i.e. same identifiers in the data matrices). Otherwise the tool will only produce the matching results, without the intensity diagnosis.
----
====================== KEY PARAMETERS ======================
**m/z Tolerance** Two ions are considered being candidates to be matched as "the same ion" only if their mass difference is below this threshold. Examples of potential relevant values by instrument type:
- Orbitrap / QTOF (high resolution): 0.005 to 0.02 Da - Triple quadrupole (standard resolution): 0.05 to 0.5 Da
**RT Tolerance** Two ions are considered being candidates to be matched as "the same ion" only if their retention time difference is below this threshold. Check the unit in your variableMetadata file: minutes or seconds.
- In minutes: typical values from 0.1 to 0.5 - In seconds: typical values from 5 to 30
**m/z and RT column names** *(column names' section)* By default, the tool looks for the ``mz`` and ``rt`` columns in your variableMetadata files. If your files use different column names (e.g. ``mass``, ``retention_time``), specify them here.
**Correlation split threshold (r)** Controls the boundary between the two analytical zoom histograms displayed in Section 5 of the report. Ions with r below this threshold appear in the lower-half zoom; ions with r at or above it appear in the upper-half zoom. Adjust this value to focus on a specific range. Examples:
- ``0.5`` (default): separates weak from moderate/strong correlations - ``0.8``: focuses the upper zoom on near-perfect correlations - ``0.0``: separates negative from positive correlations
----
====================== OUTPUT FILES ======================
**Associations.tabular** Table listing all ions from both pipelines:
- Ions shared by both pipelines (with their mass and RT differences) - Ions present only in Pipeline 1 (idWF2 column = "no match") - Ions present only in Pipeline 2 (idWF1 column = "no match")
**Quality report (PDF)** Visual report containing:
- Matching summary (how many ions paired, how many unmatched) - Heatmaps of mass and RT differences among matched ions - Intensity comparison charts (when pipelines have shared samples) - Three correlation histograms: global (20 bins, min→max), lower-half zoom (20 bins, min→split threshold), upper-half zoom (20 bins, split threshold→max).
----
====================== USAGE TIPS ======================
If **too few ions are paired**: → Gradually increase the m/z and RT tolerances to spot potentially threshold effects
If **almost all ions are paired** with small differences: → The two pipelines are very similar ✅
If **intensities differ significantly** despite good pairing: → The data pre-processing may differ between the two pipelines
